title: Understanding Your First Java Program
summary: Dissect your first milestone program line by line: understand classes, methods, and console output.
learningObjectives: Deconstruct a complete Java class and main method
Understand why the file name must match the public class name
expectedOutcomes: Ability to read, write, and explain a basic Java program without memorization

activities.title: Understanding Your First Java Program
activities.outputSnippet: Hello, World! I can write Java.

breakdown.whatIsIt: A basic Java program is composed of a class container, a main method entry point, and execution statements enclosed in curly braces.
breakdown.whyItMatters: Beginners often feel intimidated by the syntax. Once you realize every word has a single clear purpose, writing Java code becomes straightforward.
howItWorks: public class Main: In Java, all code lives inside a class (a container). The file must be named Main.java.
public static void main(String[] args): The standardized entry point where the JVM begins execution.
System.out.println("..."): Sends text to standard output (your console) and jumps to the next line.
Curly braces { }: Enclose the body of the class and the method. Every { must have a matching }.
keyTakeaways: All Java code lives inside a class
The file name must match the public class name (Main.java)
System.out.println() prints text and moves to the next line

activities.title: The Classic First Milestone
activities.description: Notice: 1. public class Main matches Main.java. 2. main() is where execution begins. 3. System.out.println prints our text string to the terminal.

questions.prompt: If a Java source file has 'public class Welcome', what MUST the file name be on disk?

hints.hint: Java is case-sensitive, and the public class name must match the file name.

questions.explanation: In Java, a public class name and its file name must match exactly, including letter casing (`Welcome.java`).

activities.title: Hands-on Practice: Write Your Milestone Program

practice.title: First Program Milestone Assignment
practice.problemStatement: Write a complete Java program that prints: 'Hello, World! I can write Java.' to standard output.
requirements: Include standard entry point: public static void main(String[] args)
Output must exactly match: Hello, World! I can write Java.
practice.expectedOutput: Hello, World! I can write Java.
hints: Remember double quotes for string literals.
End your statement with a semicolon (;).

interviewQA.question: What is the difference between System.out.println() and System.out.print()?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: System.out.print() outputs the text and leaves the console cursor on the exact same line. System.out.println() outputs the text and automatically appends a newline character, moving the cursor to the beginning of the next line.
keyPoints: print() stays on the same line
Both write to standard output stream (System.out)
commonMistakes: Thinking print() cannot output text strings

activities.title: Confidence Checklist
checklist: I can type a complete working Java program from scratch.
I know why the file name must match the class name.
I understand the difference between print() and println().
